title: Networking
tagline: From packets and sockets to HTTP, packet captures and multiplayer games
description: How computers talk across networks, and how to write programs that do it: layers and packets, IP addresses and subnets, DNS, TCP and UDP, routing, the socket API, byte order, serving many connections, HTTP by hand, URLs, a tiny web server and what TLS does, capturing and decoding packets from Ethernet up, reliable messaging over UDP with sequence numbers and acknowledgements, and the techniques behind multiplayer games: snapshots, delta compression, interpolation, client-side prediction and lag compensation. It assumes the C++ course.

milestones.title: How Networks Work
milestones.blurb: Layers and packets, IP addresses, subnets and NAT, DNS, what TCP and UDP promise, and how routing gets a packet across the world.

lessons.title: Layers and Packets
lessons.summary: Data crosses a network in packets, each wrapped in the headers of several layers - link, internet, transport and application. Encapsulation, what each layer is responsible for, the MTU that limits packet size, and why the layering lets you ignore most of the network most of the time.

lessons.title: Addresses, Subnets and NAT
lessons.summary: IPv4 addresses as 32-bit numbers, prefixes and subnet masks in CIDR notation, network and broadcast addresses, the private ranges, how NAT lets a whole home share one public address, ports, and a first look at IPv6.

lessons.title: DNS
lessons.summary: How names become addresses - the hierarchy of domains, resolvers and authoritative servers, the record types you will meet, caching and TTLs, the wire format of a DNS query with its length-prefixed labels, and why your program should call getaddrinfo instead of doing it itself.

lessons.title: TCP and UDP
lessons.summary: The two transport protocols and what each promises - TCP's connections, three-way handshake, sequence numbers, acknowledgements, retransmission, flow and congestion control and orderly close; UDP's independent datagrams with no promises at all - and how to choose.

lessons.title: Routing
lessons.summary: How a packet finds its way - the default gateway, routing tables and the longest-prefix match, hops and TTL, traceroute, and the difference between latency and bandwidth that decides how networked programs feel.

milestones.title: Sockets
milestones.blurb: The socket API, a TCP client and server, partial sends and receives, network byte order and packet layouts, serving many connections with an event loop, and UDP.

lessons.title: The Socket API
lessons.summary: Winsock, Windows' socket library - starting it up, resolving a name with getaddrinfo, creating a socket and connecting to the first address that answers, send and recv and what their return values mean, closing, and reading WSAGetLastError's error codes.

lessons.title: A TCP Client and Server
lessons.summary: The server side - bind, listen and accept - a complete echo server and client, sending everything with a loop, reading until a whole message has arrived, closing gracefully with shutdown, and the TIME_WAIT state that sometimes stops a server restarting.

lessons.title: Byte Order and Packet Layouts
lessons.summary: Network byte order is big-endian - htons, htonl and their inverses, writing and reading binary headers field by field, fields smaller than a byte packed into bit fields, why a C++ struct is the wrong tool for a wire format, and the Internet checksum.

tasks.title: A big-endian header and its checksum

lessons.title: Serving Many Connections
lessons.summary: Moving beyond one client at a time - thread per connection and its limits, non-blocking sockets and WSAEWOULDBLOCK, an event loop built on select or WSAPoll, per-connection buffers for reading and writing, and when to reach for I/O completion ports.

lessons.title: UDP Sockets
lessons.summary: Sending and receiving datagrams - sendto and recvfrom, connected UDP sockets, size limits, coping with loss, duplication and reordering, a request with timeouts and retries, checking who an answer came from, Windows' connection-reset quirk, and broadcast.

milestones.title: HTTP by Hand
milestones.blurb: How HTTP works, parsing requests and responses including chunked bodies, URLs and percent-encoding, a tiny web server that cannot be tricked into serving other files, and what TLS adds.

lessons.title: How HTTP Works
lessons.summary: The protocol of the web as plain text over TCP - a request line, headers and an optional body; a status line, headers and a body in reply - methods, status codes, the headers that matter, persistent connections, and where HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 differ.

lessons.title: Parsing HTTP Messages
lessons.summary: Reading HTTP from a byte stream - finding the end of the headers, splitting the start line and headers, case-insensitive names, finding the body's length from Content-Length or chunked transfer encoding, and the limits and strictness that keep a parser safe.

lessons.title: URLs and Encoding
lessons.summary: The parts of a URL - scheme, host, port, path, query and fragment - percent-encoding and which characters need it, query strings and form encoding, and resolving a relative link against a base URL.

lessons.title: A Tiny Web Server
lessons.summary: Putting the milestone together - routing requests by method and path with parameters, serving static files with the right Content-Type, building correct responses, and the path traversal attack that a naive file server falls for and how to stop it.

tasks.title: A router and a safe file path

lessons.title: HTTPS and TLS
lessons.summary: What TLS adds to a connection - encryption, integrity and server authentication - certificates and the chain of trust, how hostnames are matched including wildcards, the handshake in outline, SNI, and why you always use a library for it.

milestones.title: Capturing and Reading Packets
milestones.blurb: Packet capture with Wireshark, the pcap file format, Ethernet, IPv4 and IPv6, TCP and UDP headers and checksums, following a TCP conversation, and reading DNS and TLS inside captures.

lessons.title: Packet Capture
lessons.summary: Seeing the actual packets - capturing with Wireshark and Npcap, capture filters versus display filters, the pcap file format with its global and per-packet headers, and the rules about what you may capture.

lessons.title: Ethernet and IP Headers
lessons.summary: Decoding the first layers of a captured packet - the Ethernet frame with MAC addresses and EtherType, the IPv4 header field by field with its options and checksum, fragments, and the fixed 40-byte IPv6 header.

lessons.title: TCP and UDP Headers
lessons.summary: The transport headers byte by byte - UDP's eight bytes, TCP's ports, sequence and acknowledgement numbers, data offset, flags, window and options such as MSS and window scaling - and the pseudo-header both checksums cover.

tasks.title: TCP headers and the transport checksum

lessons.title: Following a TCP Conversation
lessons.summary: Turning a list of captured segments into the conversation they carry - identifying a connection by its addresses and ports, relative sequence numbers, the handshake, data in both directions, retransmissions and duplicates, and how connections end with FIN or RST.

lessons.title: Reading Protocols in Captures
lessons.summary: Going up the stack in a capture - DNS queries and answers over UDP, plain HTTP in a reassembled TCP stream, and TLS, where only the handshake is readable - the record layer, the ClientHello, and the server name in its SNI extension.

tasks.title: The server name in a TLS ClientHello

milestones.title: Reliability over UDP
milestones.blurb: Why games use UDP, sequence numbers that wrap around, acknowledgement bitfields, round-trip time estimates, resending what matters, and fragmentation and bandwidth.

lessons.title: Why Games Use UDP
lessons.summary: Why real-time games build their own protocol on UDP instead of using TCP - head-of-line blocking, the newest state making old data worthless - what a game protocol adds on top, virtual connections with timeouts, and testing under simulated loss and delay.

lessons.title: Sequence Numbers That Wrap
lessons.summary: Numbering packets with a small counter that wraps around - comparing sequence numbers correctly across the wrap with half-range arithmetic, the signed difference between two numbers, and discarding duplicates and stale packets with a sliding window.

lessons.title: Acknowledgement Bitfields
lessons.summary: Telling the sender which packets arrived without sending a packet per acknowledgement - the latest received number plus a 32-bit field for the ones before it, why the redundancy survives loss, and how the sender turns acks into "delivered" events.

lessons.title: Round Trips and Resending
lessons.summary: Measuring how long a round trip takes and smoothing it, the retransmission timeout from RFC 6298 with backoff and Karn's rule, and building reliable ordered messages on top of unreliable packets - message ids, resending until acknowledged, and delivering in order.

tasks.title: Round-trip time and the resend timeout

lessons.title: Fragmentation and Bandwidth
lessons.summary: Keeping packets under the path MTU, why IP fragmentation is avoided, splitting large blocks into fragments and reassembling them with ids, counts and timeouts, budgeting bandwidth per connection, and choosing what to send when it does not all fit.

projects.title: A reliable channel over unreliable packets

milestones.title: Multiplayer Games
milestones.blurb: The authoritative server and its tick, snapshots and delta compression, interpolation, client-side prediction and reconciliation, and lag compensation.

lessons.title: The Authoritative Server
lessons.summary: How multiplayer games are organised - the server owns the truth and clients send only inputs, why that is the basis of fair play, the fixed tick with an accumulator, tick numbers as the shared clock, and choosing tick and send rates.

tasks.title: The fixed tick and input checks

lessons.title: Snapshots and Delta Compression
lessons.summary: Sending the world to clients efficiently - what goes in a snapshot, quantising floats into a few bits, sending only what changed against a baseline the client has acknowledged, change masks, and what happens when packets are lost.

lessons.title: Interpolation
lessons.summary: Making other players move smoothly from snapshots that arrive 20 to 60 times a second with jitter and loss - rendering a little in the past, blending between the two snapshots around the render time, the size of the delay, and limited extrapolation.

lessons.title: Prediction and Reconciliation
lessons.summary: Hiding latency for your own player - running your inputs immediately with the same simulation code as the server, keeping the inputs not yet confirmed, and when the server's state arrives, resetting to it and replaying the rest; plus smoothing corrections and what cannot be predicted.

lessons.title: Lag Compensation
lessons.summary: Making hits fair when every player sees others in the past - the server keeping a short history of positions, rewinding targets to the moment the shooter saw, testing the shot there, limiting the rewind, and the trade-offs it creates for the player being shot.
